name: CARTERS

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The devil's advocate that WON on 2026-09-10 is the one I have to beat, and it was this: the entire gap is manufactured by the model's terminal growth constant. For a company whose addressable market is the number of American babies born each year, a perpetual 2% nominal growth rate is not conservative, it is wrong, and at any terminal rate at or below 0.5% Carter's was worth exactly what it cost. That argument was correct at $32.39. I re-ran it at today's price and it no longer clears: holding the $130M base and -4% explicit growth, fair value is $41.85 at the model's 2.0% terminal growth, $36.48 at 0.5%, and $35.10 at 0.0% - against a $30.69 price. Even at a HARSHER -6% explicit decline paired with ZERO terminal growth the fair value is $32.28, still above the price. So the counter that won twelve days ago loses today, on a 5% lower price plus the H1 sales and guidance data above.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Q3 fiscal 2026 operating cash flow, net of the refund tax payment and with no refund inflow - the first clean quarter in more than a year, and the number that settles whether $130M is the right base. Second, any announcement of replacement Section 122 or Section 301 duties on the relevant tariff lines, which decides the margin question.
devils_advocate.already_visible: The Q3 cash flow is not, by construction - the quarter is not reported. What IS visible and cuts against me is that H1 adjusted operating income FELL 1.3% year over year while sales rose 6.7%, so the whole of the guided full-year increase has to arrive in H2, and the Q3 guide of ~$50M against $39M is a 28% step that has not happened yet. If H2 misses, my base is too high and the verdict reverses.
devils_advocate.unresolved: I could not size the replacement tariff. The 10-Q names Section 122 and Section 301 as the likely successor authorities but neither the rate nor the timing is knowable, and that single fact decides whether the 180bp of gross margin is permanently lost or partly recovered - worth roughly $50M of operating income on $2.9B of sales, which is a third of my base. I also could not determine whether RWWM, whose accumulation prompted the rights agreement, is still building a position now that the pill has expired.

what_changed: Three things since the 2026-09-10 pass, and they move in different directions. (1) The Q2 10-Q now discloses the tariff arithmetic completely: the U.S. Supreme Court ruled IEEPA tariffs UNLAWFUL in Q1 fiscal 2026; Carter's claimed ~$130M and received ~$132M including interest, booking $128M against cost of goods sold and $4M as interest income; and REMAINING UNADJUDICATED CLAIMS ARE APPROXIMATELY $2 MILLION. The refund is over. (2) The same filing answers the question the last devil's advocate left open - whether the refunds signal the duties are being unwound - and the answer is no: the risk factors name 'the roll-back of incremental tariffs imposed under IEEPA and any additional actions taken in response to their roll-back, including tariffs imposed pursuant to Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 and tariffs imposed under Section 301', so the tariff cost is expected to be re-imposed under a different authority. (3) The trading picture improved, not deteriorated: H1 net sales rose 6.7% with all three segments growing and U.S. Retail comparable sales UP 7.8%; Q2 sales rose 5.2%; and full-year guidance is for LOW- TO MID-SINGLE-DIGIT PERCENTAGE GROWTH in adjusted operating income from $176M in fiscal 2025, with Q3 guided to ~$50M against $39M. Separately, on 2026-09-21 Carter's announced that its limited-duration stockholder rights agreement - adopted 2025-09-22 in response to rapid stock accumulation - EXPIRED in accordance with its terms, so the takeover defence is gone.
consensus_case: The market is underwriting a structural decline. Carter's sells clothing for babies in a country where fewer are being born; wholesale is roughly a third of sales and those customers cut second-half inventory commitments; tariffs cost 180bp of gross margin in Q2 and the company treats them as ongoing; the store base is shrinking (29 more closures announced in August); and the whole of the H1 cash flow improvement is a one-time tariff refund whose taxes are payable in Q3. Against that, a business earning $176M of adjusted operating income on $2.9B of sales - a 6% margin - carrying $567.8M of senior notes, is worth roughly one times sales of cash flow and no more. The market implies about -11% annual FCFF for five years, which is what a slowly liquidating brand in a shrinking end market is worth.
base_case_rationale: I keep the prior pass's $130M base and its -4% growth, because three new data points tested it and it held. The engine's $285.8M base is unusable - it is the mean of [$469.3M, $242.6M, $68.6M] where the oldest year is a post-COVID inventory unwind and the newest is the first full year of tariff cost. The current-year build: H1 fiscal 2026 operating cash flow was $202.3M, of which $132M is the refund, so ex-refund H1 CFO was $70.3M against NEGATIVE $8.3M a year earlier; H2 fiscal 2025 ran $130.6M; the income taxes on the refund (roughly $32M) are payable in Q3; capex runs ~$50M. That puts normalized free cash flow near $130M, between the $68.6M trough and the $285.8M mean. On growth I stay at -4% even though the company is now guiding adjusted operating income UP low-to-mid single digits, because the guided growth is entirely back-half weighted (H1 adjusted operating income was actually DOWN 1.3%, $46.5M against $47.1M) and because the end market - the annual US birth cohort - shrinks in real terms. What has changed is the price, not my numbers. At $30.69 the market implies -11.0% to -11.7% five-year FCFF growth on this base, a steeper decline than the bear case I can construct from the filings.
key_risks: THE RECORDED FAIR VALUE OVERSTATES: the model's terminal growth is fixed at 2.0% and I do not believe it for a shrinking birth cohort; at 0-0.5% terminal growth my own fair value is $35.10-$36.48, not the ~$42 the model will print
the base is hand-built and the name is violently base-sensitive - implied growth runs from +5% at the $68.6M trough year to -27.7% at the engine's $285.8M mean
fiscal 2027 laps the $128M cost-of-goods benefit with essentially nothing left to collect (remaining claims ~$2M)
the tariff cost is expected to return under Section 122 or Section 301; the refund was a rebate of one legal authority, not the removal of the duty
guided full-year operating income growth is entirely back-half weighted after H1 adjusted operating income fell 1.3%
watch_for: Q3 fiscal 2026 operating cash flow ex-refund and net of the refund tax payment
any Section 122 or Section 301 duty replacing the struck-down IEEPA tariffs, and at what rate
whether the Q3 guide of ~$50M of adjusted operating income against $39M is met
a 13D/13G from RWWM now that the rights agreement has expired
